title: Gen-BV
fill_note: DENSE layered wind with a jig; scorer cap 0.65
fill_how: The scored turns assume a dense, layer-by-layer wind at fill 0.65 (insulated-wire area / window; the scorer cap). Use a winding jig on a drill/lathe with a turn counter, lay each layer side-by-side with light back-tension, and do not scramble-wind: a scramble wind only reaches ≈0.55–0.60 and then the window holds fewer turns (scorer what-if `--fill 0.60` is in the table above). Never wind more than the listed turns — the copper must stay below the flanges.
steel_extra: **New steel:** Ø142 discs, M3 clamp map R30 at 0/90/180/270° and R66 at 15/165/195/345° (between neighbouring poles, outside the ring). Cut from this kit's `steel_backiron_disc.dxf`. Uses 12 of the 16 Ø20 (4 spare) and none of the Ø5.
o5_note: with 36 diametric Ø5 (R47.5/57/66.5) the scorer gives LESS (3.205 W vs 3.419 W without, same kit, scan t7 + full scores), so none are fitted
card_sub: 6 poles/rotor (12 Ø20) · 9 bobbins r39–74 × 15.7 build × 8.1 mm copper · no Ø5 · Ø142 steel · --back-iron · 2026-10-10
idea: Fewer, wider-spaced poles: 6 Ø20 per rotor (12 of the 16) on an R57 ring over nine 35.2° bobbins (r 39–74 mm, 15.7 mm build). Wider pole pitch means less pole-to-pole leakage and bigger coils, but the electrical frequency drops 25 % and 4 Ø20 sit idle; diametric Ø5 assists lowered the score here, so none are fitted. The scorer puts it at about 62 % of Gen-BR.
halb_block:
halbach_magnetisation = "none";  // NO O5 assist magnets in this kit (scan: they lower the 4-pole score)
rotor_b_same_axis   = true;     // same-index magnets share one axis: N faces S across the gap
